latin: Per sex dies geneseos habemus intelligere sex extremitates aedificii procedentes a Bresith, sicut procedunt cedri a Libano.
translator: original translation, drafted 2026-09-26 by WRITER-full-batch10, from Latin at farmer1998:17699
translation: By the six days of Genesis we are to understand the six extremities of the edifice proceeding from Bereshit, just as cedars proceed from Lebanon.
translation_note: Rendered directly from the Latin at farmer1998:17649, checked against Farmer's sense at farmer1998:17699.

sources.pico_relation: cited by Busi and Ebgi as the point of reference for the cedars-of-Lebanon gloss on the sefirot

doctrine: The thesis reads the six days of creation as the six lower sefirot, called the 'edifice', proceeding from 'Bereshit', a term Pico elsewhere treats as a symbol for the second sefirah, Hokhmah, itself read in his second, Christianizing set of Cabalistic conclusions as a figure of Christ, the Wisdom of the Father (farmer1998:17712). Farmer glosses the 'cedars of Lebanon' as the sefirot from Hesed to Yesod, and cross-references Pico's own numbering of the sefirot at thesis 11>48 (farmer1998:17760, 17766).
historiography: Busi and Ebgi print the Latin and gloss the cedars of Lebanon as the six sefirot from Hesed to Yesod, citing Recanati's commentary on Genesis (busi2014:15767). Wirszubski quotes the same Latin as the ninth conclusion of the Cabalistic set and compares it to Recanati (wirszubski1989:1675, 1678).
